newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: ANOTHER CENSURE MOTION AGAINST PROSSER
The Federal Opposition has moved another censure motion against Small Business Minister Geoff Prosser, levelling fresh allegations against him.
The Opposition moved its seventh censure motion against the minister, claiming there's further proof he has breached the ministerial code of conduct because of his business dealings.
For the third time, the Government used its majority in the House of Representatives to gag the debate.
Labor leader Kim Beazley says there are new revelations Mr Prosser actively lobbied at least two more councillors to prevent a rival development going ahead for parking reasons.
Mr Beazley called on Mr Prosser to resign immediately or for the Acting Prime Minister to sack him forthwith.

It's understood the Prime Minister's office has decided that based on the strict criteria in the code of conduct there's nothing to justify Mr Prosser going, but the minister will have to be very careful, in future about what he does.
FISCHER SAYS NATIVE TITLE BILL IS BALANCED
Acting Prime Minister Tim Fischer says the government's Wik legislation is no more and no less than what was in the government's 10-point plan, promised to farmers in May.
The government will today release the first draft of legislation to deal with the High Court's Wik decision.
Mr Fischer says the legislation will provide bucketfuls of native title for indigenous people, especially with regard to the large chunks of vacant crown land.
Mr Fischer has previously told farmers the legislation would provide bucketloads of extinguishment of native title, but he now says it won't wipe out native title across mainland Australia.
But Opposition Leader Kim Beazley says Labor is fearful the legislation won't protect all the stakeholders and will promote injustice.
TALKS TODAY OVER BHP RESTRUCTURE
Steel Unions and the ACTU are holding talks in Melbourne today with the head of BHP's steel division, Ron McNeilly, about the economic impact of the division's restructure.
BHP is closing down steel making operations in Newcastle and winding back manufacturing plants around the country at the cost of more than 3,000 jobs.
Andrew Whiley from the Australian Workers Union says thousands more jobs will be lost in service industries unless affected regions are compensated.
The Combined Steel Unions and the ACTU have launched a campaign to ensure regional economies affected by the restructure are compensated.
Mr Whiley says today's talks are focussing on Newcastle.
TORRES STRAIGHT AUTHORITY WELCOMES NEW LEGISLATION
The head of the Torres Strait Regional Authority says there's no dissatisfaction with ATSIC...despite legislation giving the authority greater autonomy.
The Federal Government yesterday passed a bill giving the authority a separate budget allocation, allowing it to bypass ATSIC and put budget submissions directly to the government.
Head of the regional authority John Abednego says it is an important move for Torres Strait.
He says it will give Torres Strait people, who want to be identified as a different indigenous race, a stronger identity.
But he says it has nothing to do with the accountability of ATSIC.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
